earlier_scan.source_named: Jungraithmayr, Herrmann 1970. Die Ron-Sprachen: Tschadohamitische Studien in Nordnigerien (includes Fyer sketch); confirmed via Ron-languages literature, no online copy found

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2003. Why reconstructing Ron is so problematic. In H. Ekkehard Wolff (ed.), Topics in Chadic Linguistics (Chadic Linguistics 1), 21-42. Köln: Rüdiger Köppe.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Section 3 Phonology (vowels, consonants, prosodies of labialisation/palatalisation) and 3.3 Tones: 'All attested Ron languages have three level tones as well as combination tones and this can therefore be posited in Proto-Ron. Tones have significant grammatical functions as well as lexical.' Nothing whatever on stress or accent; Fyer discussed only as the most conservative lect (with Tambas). downloaded from Internet Archive copy 2015-04-21 of rogerblench.info; 75-dpi image scan, scanned with tesseract at a 200-dpi render.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. n.d. Dictionary of Lis ma Run (Ron of Bokkos): draft for comment. 93 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bokkos (bokk1249), a sister Ron language, not Fyer; front matter covers parts of speech only; a full-text search for stress/accent gives nothing.

sources.citation: Decker, Ken, Fittokka Gobak, Adedamola Aregbesola, Christina Riepe, Iris Sacson, John Sacson & Samuel Eju. 2021. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the Rom (Tambas) [tdk] Language of Plateau State, Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2021-018. SIL International. 50 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Recent SIL survey of Tambas, Fyer's closest relative, with a wordlist; low chance of a stress statement but it is the only recent field report on the Fyer-Tambas branch. sil.org could not be reached by automated download to the fetcher.

sources.citation: Jungraithmayr, Herrmann (ed.). 1982. The Chad languages in the Hamitosemitic-Nigritic border area: papers of the Marburg Symposion 1979 (Marburger Studien zur Afrika- und Asienkunde A 27). Berlin: Reimer.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: archive.org text layer. Fyer occurs (22 hits) only inside the paper 'Ron-Semitic etymologies' (p. 24 ff.), which cites W. Müller's review of Die Ron-Sprachen in ZDMG 124: 215-219; no statement on Fyer stress or tone.

sources.citation: Jungraithmayr, Herrmann. 1970. Die Ron-Sprachen: Tschadohamitische Studien in Nordnigerien (Afrikanistische Forschungen III). Glückstadt: J. J. Augustin. Fyer sketch 'Die Sprache der Fyer', pp. 15-96.

sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The only descriptive treatment of Fyer; its Lautlehre for Fyer (within pp. 15-96) is where any statement on Ton/Akzent/Betonung would be. HathiTrust holds two search-only copies (mdp.39015025866669, uc1.b4234141; catalog record 000040678), so a page-level term search (Betonung, Akzent, Druck) is possible from a browser even without full view; print via ILL (OCLC 1344076).

sources.citation: Seibert, Uwe. 1997/1998. Das Ron von Daffo (Jos-Plateau, Zentralnigeria): morphologische, syntaktische und textlinguistische Strukturen einer westtschadischen Sprache. Frankfurt am Main: Peter Lang. (cited by Blench 2003 as Seibert 1997)

sources.note: Full grammar of the closest well-described Ron language (Daffo-Butura, daff1234); would give a Ron-group prosodic statement (tone vs. stress) and a bibliography of Ron work that Blench says is otherwise unpublished. Not Fyer itself.
